name: Assegno Unico Universale - SIA Project 24 25
description:
The system supports the online management of applications for the Italian
    Assegno Unico Universale (AUU), a financial benefit provided by INPS to
    families with dependent children. The considered scenario focuses exclusively
    on applications submitted directly by interested users through the INPS website,
    excluding applications submitted by delegated patronage institutions, mobile
    applications, and call-center interactions.

    An authenticated applicant can submit an AUU application as a parent,
    foster parent, or legal guardian of a child. During the first phase of the
    application, the applicant provides information about each dependent child,
    including the child's fiscal code, dependency status, disability status and,
    when applicable, disability level. Depending on the applicant type, additional
    information concerning family composition, exclusive custody, the other
    parent's fiscal code, and the requested allowance distribution between parents
    must also be provided.

    When a child's fiscal code is entered, the system verifies it in real time.
    If the child is already associated with another active application, the
    application flow is blocked and an explanatory warning is shown. The applicant
    may also specify adult dependent children who do not directly qualify for AUU
    but contribute to determining household composition. Duplicate fiscal codes for
    adult children are detected and reported.

    The amount of the allowance depends on the applicant's economic situation.
    If INPS does not already possess a valid ISEE when the application is submitted,
    the minimum allowance established by regulation is used. If a valid ISEE becomes
    available later, INPS automatically recalculates the allowance without requiring
    the applicant to modify the application.

    In the payment phase, the applicant specifies the payment method. If the
    allowance is to be divided equally between both parents, the payment information
    of the other parent must also be provided. Supported payment methods include
    credit to a SEPA IBAN account owned by the beneficiary, domiciled payment at a
    post office, and credit to an eligible prepaid card.

    Before submitting the application, the applicant must read and accept the
    declarations of responsibility and the GDPR privacy notice. The system then
    presents a summary of the entered information so that it can be reviewed.
    If validation errors are detected, the application is not submitted and the
    applicant must correct the erroneous information. If validation succeeds, the
    application is submitted and a receipt can be downloaded.

    An application may be interrupted without saving or saved as a draft before
    submission. A saved draft can later be consulted and completed. When resuming
    a draft, the applicant may either continue from the previously saved information
    or discard it and restart the application from the beginning.

    Once submitted, the application is evaluated by authorized INPS staff.
    The application may be accepted, rejected because the applicant is not entitled
    to the benefit, or suspended when additional documentation is required.
    The applicant is notified of the outcome. An accepted application remains valid
    for twelve months and the corresponding allowance is paid automatically every
    month.

    When an application is suspended, the INPS operator specifies which additional
    documents are required. The applicant can consult the application, upload the
    requested attachments, reconfirm the application data, and again accept the
    responsibility declarations and privacy notice.

    The system also allows an application originally submitted by one parent to be
    completed by the other parent. The other parent can consult the application and
    confirm or modify the proposed allowance distribution. If the applicant requested
    the entire allowance, the other parent may accept the 100 percent allocation or
    request a 50 percent distribution. When payment to the other parent is required,
    that parent provides their own payment information.

    Applicants can also add one or more children to an existing application.
    Each new child's fiscal code is checked in real time to ensure that the child
    is not already associated with another active application. After adding the
    child, existing payment and declaration data can be confirmed or modified.

    Finally, the system provides supporting functions that allow citizens to consult
    previously submitted applications, consult general information about the
    Assegno Unico Universale, and simulate the expected monthly allowance amount.

highLevelGoals: The applicant aims to successfully submit an application for the Assegno Unico Universale benefit online through the INPS website.
The applicant seeks to provide all necessary and accurate information regarding dependent children, family composition, and other required details for the AUU application.
The applicant desires to specify and manage the preferred payment method for the allowance, including providing details for the other parent if the allowance is to be divided.
The applicant needs to review all entered information, accept declarations of responsibility and privacy notice, and ensure data accuracy before final submission.
The applicant aims to save an incomplete application as a draft and later resume it to complete the submission process.
The applicant expects to be notified of the evaluation outcome of their submitted application (accepted, rejected, or suspended) and to consult its status.
The applicant needs to upload requested additional documents for suspended applications to facilitate their evaluation.
The applicant aims to add new children to an existing application and confirm or modify associated payment and declaration data.
The other parent aims to consult an AUU application originally submitted by the primary applicant.
The other parent seeks to confirm or modify the proposed distribution of the allowance, including accepting a 100% allocation or requesting a 50% distribution.
The other parent needs to provide their own payment information if they are to receive a portion of the allowance.
The citizen aims to consult general information and guidelines regarding the Assegno Unico Universale benefit.
The citizen desires to simulate the expected monthly allowance amount based on provided criteria.
The INPS Staff/Operator aims to evaluate submitted AUU applications to determine eligibility and correctness.
The INPS Staff/Operator needs to accept, reject, or suspend applications based on evaluation results and specify reasons or required documentation.
lowLevelGoals: The applicant interacts with the system to start a new application process for the Assegno Unico Universale benefit.
The applicant sends the completed and reviewed application to the INPS system for processing.
The applicant provides their personal identifying information and contact details as part of the application.
The applicant inputs information for each dependent child relevant to the AUU benefit.
The applicant modifies existing information for a dependent child within the application.
The applicant provides information about the overall family structure and household members.
The applicant attaches necessary files (e.g., ISEE declaration, identity documents) to the application.
The applicant chooses how they wish to receive the allowance (e.g., bank transfer, postal order).
The applicant inputs their bank account number (IBAN) and other necessary banking information.
The applicant indicates what portion of the allowance, if any, should be allocated to the other parent.
The applicant enters the identifying information of the other parent to facilitate allowance distribution.
The applicant requests to view a consolidated summary of all information provided before final submission.
The applicant formally agrees to the terms and conditions, taking responsibility for the accuracy of the provided data.
The applicant acknowledges and agrees to the privacy policy regarding the handling of their personal data.
The applicant explicitly verifies that all entered information is correct and complete.
The applicant stores an incomplete application to be resumed at a later time without losing progress.
The applicant requests to view all previously saved incomplete applications.
The applicant selects a particular draft application to open and continue filling out.
The applicant queries the system to check the processing stage of their application (e.g., 'submitted', 'in evaluation').
The applicant accesses the final decision regarding their application (e.g., 'accepted', 'rejected', 'suspended') and any associated reasons.
The applicant checks for alerts or messages from the system about updates to their application's status or outcome.
The applicant accesses the specific documents requested by INPS to resolve a suspended application.
The applicant submits a specific document requested by INPS to complete the evaluation of a suspended application.
The applicant updates an already submitted application by including details for a newly eligible dependent child.
The applicant updates their preferred payment method or bank details for an already submitted application.
The applicant re-affirms their declarations of responsibility and privacy notice after making changes to an existing application.
The other parent accesses the specific AUU application submitted by the primary applicant that involves them.
The other parent checks the processing status of the AUU application submitted by the primary applicant.
The other parent formally agrees to the percentage of the allowance suggested by the primary applicant.
The other parent explicitly asks for an equal split of the allowance with the primary applicant.
The other parent agrees that the primary applicant should receive the entire allowance.
The other parent inputs their banking information to receive their allocated portion of the allowance.
The citizen accesses public documentation and explanations regarding the Assegno Unico Universale.
The citizen accesses instructions and rules for applying for the Assegno Unico Universale benefit.
The citizen provides parameters such as number of children, age, and ISEE value to estimate the allowance amount.
The citizen views the estimated allowance amount calculated by the system based on their provided criteria.
The INPS staff member accesses a queue of applications awaiting review and decision.
The INPS staff member opens a particular application to view all submitted data and documents.
The INPS staff member examines the supporting files attached to an application.
The INPS staff member marks an application as approved after successful evaluation.
The INPS staff member marks an application as denied and specifies the grounds for rejection.
The INPS staff member temporarily halts an application's processing and requests further documents from the applicant.
The INPS staff member changes the application status from 'suspended' to 'in evaluation' or similar, once new documents are provided.

baselineCritiques.actors: The identified actors are accurate and cover the main roles described in the text. However, the distinction between "Applicant" and "Citizen" is somewhat redundant, as an applicant is also a citizen who can perform the supporting functions (consulting info, simulating allowance). It would be more precise to either merge them into a single "Citizen/Applicant" actor or clarify that "Citizen" refers to non-applicants using the simulation tools. Additionally, while "INPS Staff/Operator" is correctly identified, the description could be more specific about their actions (e.g., requesting documents, evaluating). Overall, the set is representative, but the separation of Applicant and Citizen is a minor conceptual overlap.
